sourceEnglishObjective: Explain why joints are staggered, using impersonal se and general rules with si
sourceEnglishSpeaking: You are the crew lead and the AI is a new hire who wants to lay shingles faster: explain how water travels across the roof, why the joints are staggered, and what happens over time if they line up, using se and si.
sourceGrammarFocus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths

sourceGrammarExamples.es: Se escalonan las juntas en cada hilera.
sourceGrammarExamples.en: The joints are staggered on every course.

sourceGrammarExamples.es: Si las juntas se alinean, el agua se mete.
sourceGrammarExamples.en: If the joints line up, water gets in.

example.target: Por eso se escalonan las juntas según el fabricante.
example.native: That's why the joints are staggered according to the manufacturer.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Impersonal se with a plural noun: se escalonan las juntas.

example.target: Si las juntas se alinean, el agua se mete.
example.native: If the joints line up, water gets in.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Si + present is used for a general truth: si se alinean, el agua se mete.

example.target: El agua busca el camino más fácil.
example.native: Water looks for the easiest path.

example.target: El viento levanta las lengüetas si la tira selladora no pega bien.
example.native: The wind lifts the tabs if the sealant strip doesn't stick well.

example.target: Se revisa el patrón en cada hilera.
example.native: The pattern is checked on every course.

sourceVerbExamples.note: Impersonal se with a singular noun: se revisa el patrón.

candidateObjective: 継ぎ目をずらす理由と水の流れを、一般条件の日本語で説明する。
candidateFocus: ～と and ～場合 express a general condition and result. ～によって attributes the pattern to the manufacturer; ～てはいけません states a site rule without a Spanish impersonal construction.

archivedForms.exampleEnglish: That's why the joints are staggered according to the manufacturer.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 継ぎ目が一直線に並ぶと、水が入ります。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: If the joints line up, water gets in.

archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Water looks for the easiest path.

archivedSpeaking.opening: 継ぎ目が一直線に並ぶと、水が入りやすくなります。メーカーの指定に従って段ごとにずらし、配置パターンを確認します。
archivedSpeaking.goal: Explain to a new hire how water travels across the roof, why joints are staggered to the manufacturer's pattern, and what can happen over time if they line up.

curriculumAdaptationNote: Current Spanish/English Master source is pinned as evidence. Archived Japanese wording is conditional candidate evidence only; trade/product/safety and Japanese/dictionary review are pending. The source grammar and verb examples are included for parity, but no selected learner/audio text or saved progress identity is created.

cards.reviewNote: To stagger is a roofing layout action; confirm the verb and manufacturer-specific offset.
Course means a row of shingles, not a training course; dictionary sense needs approval.
Tab and slot apply to a particular shingle profile; confirm terminology and system context.
Slot between tabs is profile-specific; confirm exact Japanese noun and source design.
Chalk line/墨線 can describe a marked guideline; confirm roofing trade usage.
Sealant strip and wind adhesion vary by product; confirm exact roofing sense.

cards.sourceSpanish: Si las juntas se alinean, el agua se mete.
cards.sourceEnglish: If the joints line up, water gets in.
cards.candidateJapanese: 継ぎ目が一直線に並ぶと、水が入ります。
cards.archivedJapanese: 継ぎ目が一直線に並ぶと、水が入ります。
cards.archivedEnglish: If the joints line up, water gets in.

cards.sourceSpanish: Se escalonan las juntas según el fabricante.
cards.sourceEnglish: The joints are staggered according to the manufacturer.
cards.archivedJapanese: 継ぎ目はメーカーの指定に従ってずらします。
cards.archivedEnglish: The joints are staggered according to the manufacturer.
cards.reviewNote: Manufacturer-specified staggering is an instruction; keep source specificity and await trade review.

cards.sourceSpanish: El agua busca el camino más fácil.
cards.sourceEnglish: Water looks for the easiest path.
cards.candidateJapanese: 水は通りやすい道を探します。
cards.archivedJapanese: 水は通りやすい道を探します。
cards.archivedEnglish: Water looks for the easiest path.

cards.sourceSpanish: Así no se ve la gotera hasta que es tarde.
cards.sourceEnglish: That way you don't see the leak until it's too late.
cards.candidateJapanese: そうすると、手遅れになるまで雨漏りに気づきません。
cards.archivedJapanese: そうすると、手遅れになるまで雨漏りに気づきません。
cards.archivedEnglish: That way you don't see the leak until it's too late.

cards.candidateJapanese: 見てください。お見せします。
cards.archivedJapanese: 見てください。お見せします。

cards.candidateJapanese: 理由を説明してもよろしいですか。
cards.archivedJapanese: 理由を説明してもよろしいですか。

cards.candidateJapanese: ここではそのようには施工しません。
cards.archivedJapanese: ここではそのようには施工しません。

reader.sourceSpanish: Kevin mira el techo y pregunta por qué las juntas no van en línea recta.
reader.sourceEnglish: Kevin looks at the roof and asks why the joints don't go in a straight line.
reader.candidateJapanese: ケビンは屋根を見て、なぜ継ぎ目が一直線に並んでいないのか尋ねます。
reader.archivedJapanese: ケビンは屋根を見て、なぜ継ぎ目が一直線に並んでいないのか尋ねます。
reader.archivedEnglish: Kevin looks at the roof and asks why the joints don't go in a straight line.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Mira, te lo enseño con dos tejas.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Look, I'll show you with two shingles.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「見てください。シングル材を二枚使ってお見せします。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「見てください。シングル材を二枚使ってお見せします。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Look, I'll show you with two shingles.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Si las juntas se alinean, el agua se mete.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: If the joints line up, water gets in.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「継ぎ目が一直線に並ぶと、水が入ります。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: If the joints line up, water gets in.
reader.reviewNote: If joints line up, water gets in is a source generalization; avoid treating it as a universal failure prediction.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: El agua busca el camino más fácil, y una junta abierta es el camino más fácil.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Water looks for the easiest path, and an open joint is the easiest path.
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「水は通りやすい道を探します。開いた継ぎ目は最も通りやすい道です。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「水は通りやすい道を探します。開いた継ぎ目は最も通りやすい道です。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Water looks for the easiest path, and an open joint is the easiest path.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Por eso se escalonan las juntas según el fabricante, y nunca se hace a ojo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: That's why the joints are staggered according to the manufacturer, and it's never done by eye.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「そのため、継ぎ目はメーカーの指定に従ってずらします。目分量で決めてはいけません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: That's why the joints are staggered according to the manufacturer, and it's never done by eye.
reader.reviewNote: Manufacturer offset governs; retain this condition explicitly in any final Japanese instruction.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Si una hilera tapa la junta de abajo, el agua corre por encima de la teja y sigue su camino.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: If a course covers the joint below, the water runs over the shingle and keeps going on its way.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「上の段が下の継ぎ目を覆えば、水はシングル材の上を流れていきます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: If a course covers the joint below, the water runs over the shingle and keeps going on its way.
reader.reviewNote: Course overlap and water path depend on product design; trade review required.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Pero si las ranuras quedan una encima de otra, el agua baja directo por la ranura hasta la sub-capa.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: But if the slots end up one on top of another, the water goes straight down the slot to the underlayment.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「しかし、溝が上下に重なると、水は溝を通って下葺き材へまっすぐ流れます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: But if the slots end up one on top of another, the water goes straight down the slot to the underlayment.
reader.reviewNote: Slots and underlayment describe a particular shingle system; confirm profile and wording.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Con el tiempo, la humedad llega a la madera y la gotera aparece dentro de la casa.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Over time, the moisture reaches the wood and the leak shows up inside the house.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「時間がたつと、湿気が木部に達し、家の中に雨漏りが現れます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Over time, the moisture reaches the wood and the leak shows up inside the house.
reader.reviewNote: Moisture-to-interior leak timeline is illustrative; do not present as a fixed outcome.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Así no se ve la gotera hasta que es tarde.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: That way you don't see the leak until it's too late.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「そうすると、手遅れになるまで雨漏りに気づきません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: That way you don't see the leak until it's too late.
reader.reviewNote: Too late is an absolute source phrase; confirm natural Japanese and risk framing.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: El viento también levanta las lengüetas si la tira selladora no pega bien.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: The wind also lifts the tabs if the sealant strip doesn't stick well.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「粘着帯が十分に付いていなければ、風がタブを持ち上げます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: The wind also lifts the tabs if the sealant strip doesn't stick well.
reader.reviewNote: Sealant-strip adhesion and wind uplift need product/conditions context.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Por eso se revisa el patrón en cada hilera y se traza una línea de tiza cuando hace falta.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: That's why the pattern is checked on every course and a chalk line is snapped when it's needed.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「そのため、各段の配置パターンを確認し、必要なら墨線を引きます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: That's why the pattern is checked on every course and a chalk line is snapped when it's needed.
reader.reviewNote: Pattern check and chalk-line action are site/manufacturer instructions; trade review required.

reader.sourceSpanish: La dueña de la casa escucha desde el patio y también tiene una pregunta.
reader.sourceEnglish: The homeowner is listening from the yard and also has a question.
reader.candidateJapanese: 庭で聞いていた家主にも質問があります。
reader.archivedJapanese: 庭で聞いていた家主にも質問があります。
reader.archivedEnglish: The homeowner is listening from the yard and also has a question.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Señora, ¿le puedo explicar por qué?
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Ma'am, may I explain why?
reader.candidateJapanese: ロヘリオ「理由を説明してもよろしいですか。」
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「理由を説明してもよろしいですか。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Ma'am, may I explain why?

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Si el traslape y las juntas están bien, el techo dura muchos años; si no, se filtra el agua.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: If the overlap and the joints are right, the roof lasts many years; if not, water seeps in.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「重なりと継ぎ目が適切なら屋根は長持ちしますが、そうでなければ水がしみ込みます。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: If the overlap and the joints are right, the roof lasts many years; if not, water seeps in.
reader.reviewNote: Roof longevity claim is not guaranteed; confirm source meaning and consumer-facing claim before scoring.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rogelio: Kevin, poner las juntas en línea recta es un error, y eso no se hace aquí.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rogelio: Kevin, putting the joints in a straight line is a mistake, and that's not done here.
reader.archivedJapanese: ロヘリオ「ケビン、継ぎ目を一直線に並べるのは誤りです。ここではそのようには施工しません。」
reader.archivedEnglish: Rogelio: Kevin, putting the joints in a straight line is a mistake, and that's not done here.
reader.reviewNote: Never align joints is system-specific; retain manufacturer specification and avoid universal prohibition.
